In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the wealth effects of automobile product recalls are not as great as those of drug recalls, but that the wealth losses to the shareholders of the firm with the recall are still substantial.
automobile recalls have had a significant negative impact on the wealth of the shareholders of the firm(s) with the recalled products, and also on the wealth of shareholders of competitor firms.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wealth losses to GM shareholders from the recalls of GM cars are greater than the wealth losses from the recalls of Ford or Chrysler cars.
the wealth of the automobile industry as a whole is not adversely affected by recalls.
, in general, the impact of recalls on the wealth of automobile firms and their shareholders is not as large as the Jarrell and Paltzman (1985, hereafter JP) study would lead one to expect.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the wealth losses from recalls are not borne solely by shareholders of the firm with the product recall, and that in the case of automobile recalls, the wealth losses are not borne solely or primarily by shareholders of the firms within the industry with the recalled product.
the wealth losses from product recalls may be far greater for the firms involved in the recall campaign, as well as their competitors, than the direct costs to the firms involved.
the wealth losses to the shareholders of firms with the recalled product are not significantly different from the wealth gains to shareholders of firms with nonrecalled products.
